question: Why do differentiating causes fail to establish another reality apart from this one?
premises: Differentiating causes are joined with difference.
They are considered in relation to this reality.
inference: Because another reality cannot be established, differentiating causes do not prove a separate reality beyond this one.
uncertainties: The syntactic relation of bhedāyujai to the rest of the clause is compressed.
plain_english: By causes of differentiation joined with difference, and also because another reality cannot be established, no separate reality is proved.
